verdict.rationale: The first-party GitHub README states directly that Solo 2 "also speaks OATH (TOTP/HOTP)", so the core legacy one-time-password capability is claimed. That claim is a single passing mention, with no documentation of how it works or how well. Missing for 10: slot count and provisioning workflow, a documented OATH management tool or CLI command, challenge-response (HMAC) mode, NFC/USB usage details, and independent or hands-on corroboration that OATH works.

support.subject: As a power user, the key covers legacy one-time-password schemes — TOTP/HOTP slots or challenge-response — for services that still lack WebAuthn

citations.quote: It's a USB+NFC device that protects your accounts with passkeys/WebAuthn, and also speaks OATH (TOTP/HOTP), PIV, and OpenPGP.
